I recently upgraded my computer and had to reinstall everything.  When I reinstalled RPG Maker 2003, it would not let me create a project folder in the default location.  This is because the default location (C:\Users\MyUserName\Documents\RPG Maker 2003) didn't exist, because the install didn't create an RPG Maker 2003 folder in Documents.
This was easily fixed by creating the RPG Maker 2003 folder myself.  Although I'm sure it also would've worked had I chose a folder that existed.

posts.author: jay_are
posts.body:
Will RPG Maker 2003 get a battle system fix?
The problem is very simple, and I think was fixed unofficially years ago, but it involves the battle order.
When an enemy attacks, this enemy will not even warn the player, it will just attack suddenly, which is really hard to follow because it feels like too many things are happening at once.
In the database / system, there's the "Enemy Attack" sound effect. This, in RPG Maker 2000, would have served as a warning before a monster attacks, so to keep the flow of battle smooth and organized, 1 step at a time. But in 2003, even though this same sound is in the database, the programmers seem to have forgotten to make it work in battle.
This has caused the battle system to be messed up in every RPG Maker 2003 game ever made since 2003, and if that's not the saddest thing, no one bothered to care until it was fixed unofficially some years ago, but we need it fixed in the official program!

posts.author: Topaz Light
posts.body:
So, I've actually noticed a different oddity in each engine, both related to Name Input Processing. Neither are remotely game-breaking, fortunately, but I still feel they warrant mention.
RPG Maker 2003's is simpler to describe, so it'll go first; the "space" character is un-inputtable. It won't let the player enter it as part of an Actor's name despite it being totally functional when entered in the editor to be used as part of an Actor's default name. It plays the "confirm" sound effect when clicked on, but the space is not added to the current string of characters comprising the entered name, and does not count against the twelve-character limit. It just... doesn't enter anything. I have tested both engines and this error is
not
present in RPG Maker 2000, just 2003.
However, RPG Maker 2000 has its
own
error that isn't present in RPG Maker 2003, and, wouldn't you know it, it's related to the 12-character limit for Actor names. I was kind of hesitant to report this, actually, since it's harmless from what I can tell, easy enough to accommodate if you know about it, and actually kind of cool, but...
RPG Maker 2000's Name Input Processing actually allows you to enter
thirteen
characters for an Actor's name. The thirteenth character is invisible, and moves the selection highlighter over onto the window boundary, but it's registered as part of the name just fine, and the thirteen-character name you entered will be printed completely normally with no issues when it's called in dialogue or menus. It doesn't even overlap with the "LV" marker in the Skills section of the party menu; it presses right up against it, but it doesn't overlap, and it doesn't cause any problems elsewhere in the party menu, either, that I can see. As I mentioned before, it's completely harmless, and personally I think it's actually kind of a cool little oddity that I almost don't
want
to have fixed, because it'd make for a nifty little secret trick in RPG Maker 2000 games. I do think it should be known about, though, at least. Interestingly, the Actor name limit in the editor is still twelve characters, so the only way to get an Actor with a thirteen-character-long name is to enter one in-game via Name Input Processing.

posts.author: Topaz Light
posts.body:
Alright, so, I don't know if this is a bug or just something that's ingrained into how the engines work, but, if a Common Event is called in mid-movement (most likely via key input processing) onto a "Player Touch" event set to be above or below the player, that Common Event will happen
instead
of the event the tile of which is being moved onto. The event assigned to the tile does not simply wait for the Common Event to finish before activating itself; it just doesn't activate at all. I've tested this in both 2000 and 2003, and it happens in both. The primary issue is obviously that this would potentially be very abusable; players who know how to take advantage of it could use it to do things like bypass soft boundaries in areas and sequence-break or screw up events that were set up to transition smoothly from gameplay.
I don't actually know what the cause of this is, or how easy it would be to fix, but it causes issues for things like run button scripts, and it was actually brought up in
my Run Button script tutorial
. I understand this is likely not gonna be nearly so quick and easy a fix as the Name Input Processing things, but I feel confident that this is something that's going to cause problems for people who want to smoothly integrate custom gameplay elements into the controls of their games, and therefore something that warrants addressing, if it's at all possible. I'll confess that this report is partially self-serving and may be asking a little much, but I still feel like it's something that should be known, as obscure as it is.

posts.author: Cherry
posts.body:
Thank you for this report, I'll note it down. Actually, I was aware that there is
some
old and well-known problem with event-controlled movement onto player touch events, but I didn't have an exact description of the circumstances like this before. However, I heard that the solution for circumventing this problem is to change the "player touch" event to "event touch". It shouldn't make much difference for stationary events like teleports - but it may make a difference for moving events if they are not designed to initiate player interaction on their own (without the player actively moving towards them).
(About the abusability, though: If a player knows about these kinds of flaws in the RM engine, there is a high chance they also know how to start the game in test play mode and then just use Ctrl to walk through walls and such.)

posts.author: Psychotic_Hero
posts.body:
I found some bugs with adding a new Mage character.
I am using rm2k3 v1.12a
I'll go step by step for a recreation of the crash.
I opened Database, increased maximum number by one, typed a character name, added a stock graphic, stock charset, stock Animation Mage (female), change class to Mage B, click apply and the skills/spells populated on the right, set parameter curves to all inferior, clicked on Battle Test, set character level to 30 and when I tried to cast Blind, the game crashes with the error "Invalid CBDATA was specified."
I know the guide said to check the Battle Animations to make sure they're set. When I clicked on the Skills tab, clicked on Blind, clicked on Animation, clicked on Set, I clicked on the newly made Mage character and saw that the Animation was working, Choose Default CBA was already set to Skill. I hit cancel and I clicked on Battle Test again. I tried casting Blind and the game crashed with the same error.
I ended up with finding a fix. I went back to the Skills tab, clicked on Blind, click on Animation, clicked on Set, clicked on the newly made Mage character, saw the Animation was working, Choose Default CBA was still set to Skill and I click OK.  I clicked Apply and then ran the Battle Test again. I ended up casting Blind just fine. I tried casting other spells but the game crashed, so I went ahead and click on each spell, click on the new Mage, and clicked OK for each one and the game never crashed since. It just seemed so misleading when I initially checked the Skills tab for the spells assigned to the Mage by class.
Also, I did find out when you do make a new character, the character automatically gets checked marked for all weapons, armor, and equipment in the Items tab under Equipment settings. It gets annoying to uncheck the new character from each weapon/equipment.
Perhaps you could make it so that new characters aren't automatically assigned?

I'm not sure if this is a bug, but it is something strange I noticed.
RPG Maker 2003 1.12a: When editing Troops in the Database, the condition to trigger a Battle Event when the player or enemy's HP is between a certain percent seems to only sometimes trigger right away when the condition is met, while other times there's a delay where it only happens after another character uses a move. After editing various different things to try and find out what's causing it, the cause seems to be the amount of frames of the animation that causes the condition to be met. But even then it's not a guarantee since sometimes the event will trigger regardless. I've made a video showcasing this here:
However, in the unofficial version of RPG Maker 2003, the event triggers immediately 100% of the time as far as I can tell.
Another note about the fullscreen issue in RPG Maker 2000 1.62 that I posted about earlier: It seems to work the same way as the "DirectDraw (for older machines)" setting in the video options of RPG Maker 2003 1.12a. I can just use GDI, but there's no such option in 2000. Though I still find it strange that the unofficial versions of both 2000 and 2003 worked fine in fullscreen, even on my modern(-ish) machine, yet the official ones don't (outside of GDI mode in 2003).

posts.author: TheArtOfScarecrows
posts.body:
whydoihavetosignup said:
I'm not sure if this is a bug, but it is something strange I noticed.
RPG Maker 2003 1.12a: When editing Troops in the Database, the condition to trigger a Battle Event when the player or enemy's HP is between a certain percent seems to only sometimes trigger right away when the condition is met, while other times there's a delay where it only happens after another character uses a move. After editing various different things to try and find out what's causing it, the cause seems to be the amount of frames of the animation that causes the condition to be met. But even then it's not a guarantee since sometimes the event will trigger regardless. I've made a video showcasing this here:
However, in the unofficial version of RPG Maker 2003, the event triggers immediately 100% of the time as far as I can tell.
Click to expand...
Can confirm this bug, it's been making eventing troops infuriating. The only consistent workaround is to make skills used by the player have a minimum of 24 frames for their animations.
The reason this bug sometimes doesn't happen is because this bug only applies to the player using skills. Using a basic attack does not have the bug happen.

posts.author: Dyluck
posts.body:
Not sure if anyone still checks this thread, but here's a few things I found over the years. Version 1.12a
1) I've discovered a bug in rm2k3 where sometimes when a battler steps forward to use a skill, they don't step back into line afterwards. So far it seems it happens whenever you use any skill that changes your own State in any way, both inflicting or removing any state.
2) The exact same skill learned by 2 different actors have different spacing, because 1 actor learned from their Actor skill list, while the other learned via a Class skill list. Seems the string used in Terms tab already adds a space after skill name by default, while the one for Classes seems to not.
3) Basically in RM2K3 after using a skill in battle, sometimes the cursor starts at a different skill on the next turn, instead of the last skill used. The reason is that the cursor will move down by a number determined by ALL skills  the hero has, instead of what skills are in the current skill command window. So for example if your database has these skills:
Fire 1 (Magic)
Fire 2 (Magic)
Fire 3 (Magic)
Heal 1 (Priest)
Heal 2 (Priest)
Heal 3 (Priest)
...and your hero has all 6 skills and both the Magic and Priest command. Then if you use Heal 2 in battle for example, the cursor will see this at the 5th entry of all your skills, and so it will move down 5 spots in every skill window. So in the Magic window, the cursor ends up pointing at Fire 3. In the Priest window, the cursor ends up on Heal 3. This gets even more messy when you have same type skills that may not be listed together in the database, or some field only or dummy skills that don't show up in battle, etc.
4) If your skill has an Attack Element that is a weapon type, then you need to be equipped
with that type of weapon to use the skill. Makes sense. But if you tick the Reduce
Resistance checkbox, suddenly you can use the skill without equipping that weapon type.
And like the thing is, even if I pretend this is just a skill that "reduces Distance resistance", and doesn't require a Distance weapon to be equipped, if the skill does any damage, it is still in-fact doing Distance type damage,
even if I'm equipped with a dagger!!
5) I find that enemies are refusing to use skills that give themselves Stat x2 state... Because apparently enemies refuse to use any skill that ONLY inflicts a STATE on themselves. So you MUST either tick any one of the boxes for stat increase, even if you only set the value to zero, like HP increase = 0, OR you need to tick one of the boxes for elemental defense resistance. Otherwise, the enemies will NEVER execute that skill.
Bonus Fact: A skill that increases/decreases a stat (such as HP) by 0 will result
in a change of more than 0 if the skill also has say a Magic Rate (Influence) of
1 or more (which it needs to be if you want the skill to be affected by something
like Silence). Apparently rm2k3 doesn't know how or want to multiply by a base
value of 0.
